mechanism: Displacement from the Second World War left millions of refugees across Europe, and the UN created UNHCR in 1950 to handle them.
Nazi persecution produced stateless survivors and refugees whom the new agency was mandated to protect and resettle.
Seljuk conquest of Anatolia and Jerusalem threatened Byzantium and pilgrim access, prompting Byzantine appeals and Urban II's call to crusade.
The 1054 schism estranged Rome and Constantinople, shaping papal willingness to answer Byzantine appeals for military help.
Fatimid retaking of Jerusalem from the Seljuks in 1098 changed the Holy Land's balance of power just before the crusaders arrived.
Third-century civil wars and fiscal collapse weakened Rome's Rhine and Danube frontiers, opening the empire to migrating peoples.
Goths who crossed the Danube in 376 revolted against Roman mistreatment, forcing Rome to accept Gothic settlement inside the empire.
Marcomannic invasions of the 160s and 170s pushed Germanic groups toward the Roman frontier, an early phase of later migrations.
Germanic federate armies seized Italy, and Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus in 476, ending the Western Roman Empire.
Visigoths settled in Aquitaine and Hispania under Roman federate treaties, founding a successor kingdom on former imperial land.
Theoderic's Ostrogoths conquered Italy in 493 and founded a kingdom on former Roman territory.
Vandals crossed into North Africa in 429 and seized Carthage in 439, founding a kingdom in former Roman provinces.
Rehoboam's refusal of northern demands split the united monarchy around 930 BCE, creating Judah as a separate southern kingdom.
Shoshenq I's campaign against Judah around 925 BCE plundered Jerusalem's temple and royal treasuries, weakening the young kingdom.
Zedekiah's revolt against Babylon provoked Nebuchadnezzar's siege, which destroyed Jerusalem in 587-586 BCE and ended the kingdom.
Judah's rebellion against Babylon brought Nebuchadnezzar's 597 BCE siege, which deported King Jehoiachin and the leading citizens.
Babylon's deportation of Judean elites created the exile community whose experience of loss shaped Jewish religious identity.
Mobile email on NTT DoCoMo's i-mode service created demand for expressive pictograph characters, which the company's designers devised in 1999.
Crusader control of Jerusalem created dangerous pilgrim routes, and in 1119 nine knights founded the Templar order to protect them.
Soviet aid, including Japanese arms seized in Manchuria in 1945, equipped Chinese Communist forces and shaped the war's outcome.
Japan's 1937-1945 invasion weakened Nationalist armies and let Communist forces expand, setting the stage for the civil war's renewal in 1946.
Napoleonic rule reorganized Italian states and spread liberal and national ideas that later fueled the Risorgimento.
Revolutionary French armies carried ideas of popular sovereignty into Italy, inspiring patriots to seek a unified state.
The 1815 Vienna settlement restored Austrian control over northern Italy and kept the peninsula divided, creating the grievance unification addressed.
Mazzini and other nationalist writers made a unified Italian nation-state the central political goal of the Risorgimento.
Piedmontese-led campaigns and plebiscites in 1860-61 created the Kingdom of Italy under Victor Emmanuel II.
Soviet authorities created the Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic in 1936 as a constituent republic of the Soviet Union.
The 1917 revolution brought the Bolsheviks to power, and their Soviet state later delimited Kazakh territory into union republics.
Bolshevik victory in the Russian Civil War secured Central Asian territory, allowing Soviet authorities to create the Kazakh autonomous republic in 1920.
The Taliban regime sheltered al-Qaeda and refused to surrender Osama bin Laden after 9/11, prompting the US-led invasion of 2001.
The Soviet occupation and its 1989 withdrawal left armed networks and a fragmented Afghan state that the Taliban later exploited.
The 2001 invasion overthrew the Taliban, and US-backed governance produced the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan in 2004.
Cross-border militancy from the Afghan war spilled into Pakistan's tribal areas, fueling insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa from 2004.
NATO's 1999 Kosovo intervention and the West's later recognition of Kosovo gave Moscow a precedent it cited to justify action in Georgia.
Soviet-era autonomy arrangements for South Ossetia and Abkhazia left unresolved status disputes that erupted into conflict in 2008.
The pro-Western Orange Revolution in Ukraine heightened Russian fears of NATO encroachment, hardening Moscow's stance toward Georgia.
Rome's conquest of the Samnites extended its control across central Italy, making it a Mediterranean power that would clash with Carthage.
Rome's 338 BCE victory over the Latin League consolidated its hegemony over Latium, a precondition for its later overseas expansion.
Victory in the Punic Wars gave Rome control of the western Mediterranean, the foundation of the expansion that produced the Roman Empire.
Philip V of Macedon's alliance with Hannibal drew Rome into the Macedonian Wars, extending Roman power into Greece.
Carthage's unpaid mercenaries revolted after the First Punic War's defeat, prompting a bitter three-year uprising.
Numidian prince Masinissa switched to Rome in the Second Punic War, gaining Roman backing that expanded Numidian power.
The Bolshevik seizure of power in 1917 enabled the Soviet declaration of a Byelorussian republic in 1919.
The 1919-1921 Polish-Soviet War fixed Belarus's western frontier with Poland, determining the territory the Soviet republic governed.
Cyrus II of Anshan overthrew Astyages of Media around 550 BCE and absorbed the Median realm into the new Persian polity.
Cyrus's conquest of Babylon in 539 BCE added the Neo-Babylonian realm and its administration to Persian rule.
Persian expansion into the Aegean, and Darius's and Xerxes' campaigns to punish Athens and Eretria, led to the Greco-Persian Wars.
Cyrus's 538 BCE edict let exiled Judeans rebuild the Temple, which was completed under Persian sponsorship in 516 BCE.
Darius I organized the empire into provinces run by satraps, an administrative model later adopted by Hellenistic states.
Faraday's 1831 discovery that changing magnetic fields induce current made rotating electromagnetic generators possible.
Dynamo-driven central power, as in Edison's 1882 Pearl Street system, supplied electric lamps and made commercial incandescent lighting practical.
Miniaturized transistors on integrated circuits let Intel engineers place a complete central processor on a single chip in 1971.
Decades of mainframe computing created the logic-design demand that microprocessors condensed onto a single chip.
Affordable programmable processors made home consoles practical, beginning with Fairchild's F8-based Channel F in 1976.
Microprocessors supplied the computing power that let handheld mobile phones add features and shrink from the 1980s onward.
Einstein's 1905 special relativity showed that a body's inertia depends on its energy content, yielding E=mc2 as a consequence.
Maxwell's electromagnetic theory, confirmed by Hertz's experiments, supplied the radiation framework Einstein used for the energy-inertia argument.
Electric generators let wind rotors produce electricity, as Charles Brush's 1887 turbine in Cleveland demonstrated.
Xerxes' 480 BCE invasion of Greece brought a Persian army to the pass, making the Greek stand at Thermopylae unavoidable.
The Persian Empire's campaigns to punish Greek revolt-supporters and expand its rule drove the invasion that reached Thermopylae.
The 1997 Treaty of Amsterdam incorporated the Schengen acquis into EU law, binding member states to its border-free arrangements.
German reunification in 1990 prompted France and others to bind a unified Germany into deeper integration, shaping Maastricht's terms.
The Schengen project's 1985 border-free model built momentum for deeper European integration, which Maastricht codified.
Maastricht's institutional structure was revised at the 1997 Treaty of Amsterdam, which reorganized EU decision-making.
Earthquake-damaged sanitation let cholera, introduced through a UN peacekeeping camp, spread across Haiti from October 2010.
Enlightenment ideas of reason, science and secular government reshaped European thought, and historians date modern history from this shift.
Yuan rule weakened Goryeo's independence, and the Ming overthrow of the Yuan in 1368 cleared the way for Yi Seong-gye's 1392 founding of Joseon.
Ming recognition of Yi Seong-gye as Korean king in 1392 legitimized the new Joseon state and anchored its tributary foreign policy.
Third Republic diplomacy built the 1892 Franco-Russian alliance, which became the core of the 1907 Triple Entente with Britain.
The Viet Minh's war against France ended with the 1954 Geneva Accords, which left a communist-led Democratic Republic in the North.
Japan's occupation and 1945 surrender let Ho Chi Minh's Viet Minh seize Hanoi and proclaim the Democratic Republic of Vietnam.
Ho Chi Minh led the Viet Minh and proclaimed the Democratic Republic of Vietnam in 1945, founding the state that became North Vietnam.
Chinese Communist victory in 1949 gave the Viet Minh a friendly border state and military aid during the First Indochina War.
Revolutionary France's client Batavian Republic took over the bankrupt VOC's territories in 1800, creating the Dutch East Indies colonial state.
Volta's 1800 battery gave Faraday a steady current source, which he used in his 1831 experiments detecting induced currents.
Sturgeon's 1825 electromagnet allowed strong magnetic fields to be controlled, a tool Faraday then used in his induction experiments.
Faraday's induction principle became the operating basis of the transformer, which Gaulard and Gibbs commercialized in the 1880s.
Maxwell built his field theory on Faraday's induction law, and Hertz's 1886 experiments confirmed the electromagnetic waves it predicted.
Protestant challenges to papal authority from 1517 forced the Catholic Church to define doctrine and reform its institutions.
Spanish Habsburg rulers, especially Philip II, became the Catholic Counter-Reformation's main political sponsors across their empire.
Habsburg Catholic reassertion in Bohemia and the Empire provoked the 1618 Prague revolt that grew into the Thirty Years' War.
Philip II's Catholic enforcement and Inquisition in the Netherlands drove the Dutch revolt that became the Eighty Years' War.
Militant Catholic opposition to Huguenot toleration fueled France's religious wars from 1562 onward.
The Crimean War drained British troops and money from India, weakening the East India Company's garrisons before the 1857 uprising.
After the uprising, Parliament transferred governance from the East India Company to the Crown in 1858, establishing direct British rule.
Soviet domination through Stalinist rule and the Warsaw Pact left Hungary's communist government unpopular, sparking the 1956 uprising.
Soviet-backed Stalinist rule had stalled Czechoslovakia's economy, prompting the reform program that Dubček launched in 1968.
The Soviet crushing of Hungary's 1956 uprising reshaped Eastern Bloc reform debates, influencing Czechoslovak leaders' cautious liberalization.
Overseas exploration and colonization linked distant economies and states, reshaping European commerce and politics in the early modern era.
Renaissance humanism revived classical learning and reshaped European culture, opening the intellectual world of the early modern era.
Gutenberg's movable-type printing spread books and ideas across Europe, accelerating religious and scientific change in the early modern era.
The Black Death's population collapse raised wages and weakened feudal labour obligations, undermining medieval social structures.
The 184 CE Yellow Turban uprising collapsed central Han authority and empowered regional warlords, fragmenting the empire.
Sun Quan and Liu Bei's 208 defeat of Cao Cao at Red Cliffs blocked his southern unification and fixed the tripartite division.
Cao Cao's 200 victory at Guandu over Yuan Shao gave him control of northern China, the base of the Wei kingdom.
Fatimid-led Kutama Berber forces overthrew the Aghlabid emirate in 909, opening Ifriqiya to the new Fatimid state.
Abbasid decline and fragmentation let Ismaili Shi'a missionaries build the Kutama base that founded the rival Fatimid caliphate.
The Zanj Rebellion of 869-883 drained Abbasid resources and exposed central weakness that rival movements exploited.
Fatimid withdrawal to Egypt in 972 left Zirid governors in Ifriqiya, who became effectively independent rulers.
Saladin's campaign ended the Fatimid Caliphate in 1171 and established the Ayyubid dynasty in Egypt.
The revolt against Spanish Habsburg rule, fought as the Eighty Years' War, produced the Republic when the northern provinces declared independence in 1581.
The 1579 Union of Utrecht bound the northern provinces together, providing the political foundation for the Republic's independence.
Calvinist Protestantism gave the northern revolt religious cohesion and shaped the Republic's Reformed church and political culture.
The Dutch Republic's maritime commerce and the 1602 founding of the Dutch East India Company built the overseas Dutch colonial empire.
Commercial rivalry with England over trade routes and fisheries led to the Anglo-Dutch Wars of the 1650s to 1670s.
Commercial prosperity of the Dutch Republic created a large market for paintings that defined the Dutch Golden Age.
Germanic migrations into Gaul in the fifth century brought Frankish groups into Roman territory, creating the settlements that became Francia.
The collapse of Roman authority in northern Gaul after 476 left space for Clovis's Frankish kingdom to expand.
Clovis's 486 conquest of the Roman-ruled Soissons realm gave the Franks control of northern Gaul, the nucleus of Francia.
Pepin the Short's 751 coup replaced the Merovingian kings, and Carolingian rule grew into the Carolingian Empire by 800.
The 843 Treaty of Verdun split Francia, creating West Francia, which became the basis of the later kingdom of France.
The 843 Treaty of Verdun split Francia, creating East Francia, the core of the later German kingdom.
Timur's conquests from the 1370s built the Transoxanian and Iranian realm that his descendants ruled as the Timurid state.
The Ilkhanate's collapse in 1335 fragmented Iran and Central Asia, creating the power vacuum Timur exploited.
Genghis Khan's Mongol conquests reshaped Central Asia and gave Chinggisid legitimacy that Timur later claimed.
Dennis Gabor invented holography in 1947 while trying to correct lens aberrations in electron microscopes.
Spacewar! on university computers inspired Nolan Bushnell's 1971 Computer Space, the first commercial video game, and the console designers who followed.
Germans besieging Acre in 1190 founded a hospital brotherhood during the Third Crusade, which became the Teutonic Order.
The Crusading movement's papal legitimacy and demand for religious knightly service shaped the Order's military and charitable mission.
The Knights Templar's combination of monastic vows and military service provided the model that the Teutonic Knights adopted.
The Teutonic Knights' Prussian Crusade from the 1230s conquered and Christianized the Baltic Prussians, creating the Order's state.
Abbasid caliphs such as al-Mu'tasim built military forces from enslaved Turkic soldiers, creating the mamluk institution.
William's claim to the English throne and his invasion force led Harold's army to confront him at Hastings in 1066.
Muhammad led the Muslim community against the Meccan army at Badr, making it the first major battle between the two sides.
Badr's victory raised the Muslim community's standing in Arabia, strengthening its position in the 628 Treaty of al-Hudaybiya.
